concepts.name: Constitutional Basis of the 11th Schedule: Article 243G vs. 243D
key_dimensions: Article 243G empowers state legislatures to devolve powers — it is enabling, not mandatory (UPSC trap: devolution is discretionary, not automatic)
Distinction between Article 243G (powers/authority) and Article 243D (reservation of seats) — both relate to Panchayats but serve different purposes
Why 11th Schedule has 29 subjects while 12th Schedule has 18 subjects — structural comparison
74th Amendment (municipalities) vs. 73rd Amendment (Panchayats) — parallel architecture and which schedule applies to which

concepts.name: Agriculture and Agricultural Extension as a Devolved Subject
key_dimensions: Scope: includes land improvement, soil conservation, watershed management — distinguishing overlaps with Union and State List entries
Agricultural extension vs. agricultural research — extension is in 11th Schedule; research often remains with state/central agencies (ICAR)
Overlap with Minor Irrigation (subject 3) and Land Improvement (subject 2) — UPSC frequently tests subject-boundary confusion
Why Minimum Support Price (MSP) and procurement are NOT part of 11th Schedule — central government domain

concepts.name: Land Reform and Land Consolidation as Panchayat Subjects
key_dimensions: Subject 2 (Land improvement) vs. Subject 1 (Agriculture) — where land reforms fit and why this is a politically sensitive devolution
Tension between state land revenue departments retaining control vs. Panchayat empowerment
Land records digitization and its link to Panchayat functions — contemporary relevance
Distinction: 'Land reforms' in directive principles (Article 39) vs. 11th Schedule devolution — different constitutional planes

concepts.name: Minor Irrigation, Water Management, and Watershed Development
key_dimensions: Subject 3 specifically covers minor irrigation — major and medium irrigation remain with states (UPSC trap on jurisdiction boundaries)
Watershed development as an overlap between subjects 3 and 1 — how states resolve this in practice
Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) linkage — how central schemes align with devolved subjects
Groundwater regulation: whether it falls under minor irrigation subject or remains with states — a gray area

concepts.name: Animal Husbandry, Dairying, and Poultry under the 11th Schedule
key_dimensions: Subject 4 — scope includes veterinary services, breed improvement; distinguishing from animal welfare laws (central)
Overlap with public health (Subject 23) when animal diseases have zoonotic potential
NDDB, cooperative dairies (Amul model) vs. Panchayat role — institutional overlap
Why slaughterhouses (Subject 15) are listed separately from animal husbandry — UPSC tests this distinction

concepts.name: Fisheries as Subject 5: Scope and Limitations
key_dimensions: Freshwater/inland fisheries vs. marine fisheries — 11th Schedule covers inland; marine fisheries involve Union jurisdiction (Exclusive Economic Zone)
Fisheries vs. fishing rights — constitutional distinction between livelihood subject and rights subject
Overlap with minor water bodies (tanks, ponds) which may be managed by Panchayats for both irrigation (Subject 3) and fisheries (Subject 5)
Blue Revolution scheme and its intersection with devolved fisheries subject

concepts.name: Social and Farm Forestry, Minor Forest Produce
key_dimensions: Subject 6: Social forestry and farm forestry — distinguished from Reserved Forests under Indian Forest Act (state subject, not devolved)
Minor Forest Produce (MFP) — overlap with Forest Rights Act 2006 (Gram Sabha powers) vs. 11th Schedule devolution
PESA Act 1996: how it extends Panchayat (specifically Gram Sabha) authority over minor forest produce in scheduled areas
Difference: 'Social forestry' (plantations on degraded land) vs. 'community forestry' under Joint Forest Management — institutional roles

concepts.name: Small-Scale Industries and Khadi/Village Industries
key_dimensions: Subject 8: Small scale industries including food processing — Panchayat's role vs. MSME Ministry's domain
Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) — central statutory body — tension with devolved subject 9 (Khadi, village and cottage industries)
UPSC trap: Subjects 8 and 9 are separate entries — small scale industries ≠ cottage industries
One District One Product (ODOP) scheme and alignment with these devolved subjects

concepts.name: Rural Housing: Subject 10 and Its Institutional Linkages
key_dimensions: Rural housing as a Panchayat subject vs. implementation through central schemes (PMAY-Gramin) — who actually controls funds
Distinction between urban housing (12th Schedule, Subject 2) and rural housing (11th Schedule, Subject 10)
Role of District Rural Development Agencies (DRDAs) vs. Panchayats in housing scheme implementation — a classic devolution failure case
Indira Awaas Yojana (now PMAY-G) — beneficiary selection role of Gram Sabha as operationalization of Subject 10

concepts.name: Drinking Water as Subject 11: Devolution vs. Central Schemes
key_dimensions: Subject 11 explicitly lists drinking water — one of the most critical subjects but also most under-devolved in practice
Jal Jeevan Mission: centrally sponsored, implemented through states/Panchayats — how central schemes override devolved authority
Drinking water vs. sanitation (Subject 23) — two separate entries, UPSC frequently tests whether they are one or two subjects
Water quality monitoring — who is responsible under the 11th Schedule framework? (institutional gap)

concepts.name: Fuel and Fodder as a Devolved Subject
key_dimensions: Subject 12: Fuel and fodder — often overlooked but tests conceptual completeness of the 29-subject list
Link to common property resources (CPRs) — grazing lands, village commons managed by Panchayats
Overlap with social forestry (Subject 6) when fodder trees are involved
Declining CPRs in India — empirical dimension showing gap between constitutional devolution and ground reality

concepts.name: Roads, Culverts, Bridges, Ferries — Subject 13
key_dimensions: Subject 13 covers rural connectivity infrastructure — distinction from national/state highways (not devolved)
PMGSY (Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana) — centrally sponsored but linked to this devolved subject

concepts.name: Non-Conventional Energy Sources: Subject 14
key_dimensions: Subject 14 (Non-conventional energy sources) is uniquely forward-looking — relevant to solar/wind energy devolution debates
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) vs. Panchayat authority — central programs often bypass local bodies

concepts.name: Poverty Alleviation Programmes: Subject 16

Social audit under MGNREGA as an expression of Gram Sabha oversight — connects Article 243A (Gram Sabha) with Subject 16

concepts.name: Education: Primary and Secondary Schools under Subject 17
key_dimensions: Subject 17 covers education including primary and secondary schools — but Right to Education Act (central law) overlaps significantly

concepts.name: Libraries as Subject 20: Cultural and Educational Dimension
key_dimensions: Subject 20 (Libraries) — often ignored but tests completeness of 11th Schedule knowledge
Village libraries vs. district libraries — which fall under Panchayat jurisdiction
Cultural activities as implicit in library function — overlap with cultural dimension of local governance

concepts.name: Health and Sanitation: Subject 23 — Scope and Overlaps
key_dimensions: Subject 23: Health and sanitation including hospitals, primary health centres, dispensaries — broad scope

National Health Mission (NHM) — Village Health Sanitation and Nutrition Committees (VHSNCs) as Gram Sabha sub-committees operationalizing Subject 23

concepts.name: Family Welfare as Subject 25: Population Policy Dimension
key_dimensions: Subject 25 explicitly lists family welfare — connects Panchayats to population stabilization goals

concepts.name: Women and Child Development: Subject 26

concepts.name: Maintenance of Community Assets: Subject 29 — The Final Subject
key_dimensions: Subject 29 is a residual/catch-all provision: maintenance of community assets — often tested as the last and most flexible subject
